description: test_no_human_touch.py:test_no_elevated_privilege (line 86-89) asserts `'sudo' not in txt.lower()` over the .sh source. This is a substring check that will also flag legitimate words containing 'sudo' (e.g. 'pseudo', 'pseudo-tty', a comment mentioning 'no sudo allowed'). It also IGNORES the case where elevation is requested via `osascript -e 'do shell script ... with administrator privileges'` (osascript IS pattern-checked, but only as a literal word — `/usr/bin/osascript` invocation is caught). Conversely, `pkexec`, `doas`, `security execute-with-privileges`, `AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges` are NOT in HUMAN_TOUCH_PATTERNS, so a future regression that elevates via any of these mechanisms passes the test. Either tighten to `\bsudo\b` regex and add the other escalation primitives to HUMAN_TOUCH_PATTERNS, or document the limit explicitly.

evidence.snippet:
HUMAN_TOUCH_PATTERNS = [
    r"\bosascript\b",
    ...
    r"\bsudo\b",
    ...
]
...
def test_no_elevated_privilege():
    for src in (INSTALL_SH, PLIST_RENDER_PY):
        txt = _read(src)
        assert "sudo" not in txt.lower(), f"sudo found in {src}"
